title: Build a business directory backend
prompt: In this Express business directory app, I need a persistent database and API that my mobile frontend can use. Let visitors search and view businesses by location, category, and keywords. Let business owners register, create listings, edit listings they own, and request ownership of existing listings without immediately granting access. Let signed-in users rate and review businesses and bookmark favorite places. Add appropriate validation, authorization, database setup and migrations, and tests for search and ownership rules. Include a step-by-step guide for running the database and backend locally and connecting the frontend, with example API requests.

title: Build a location-based business directory backend
prompt: In this Express TypeScript app, I need a database-backed API for a location-based business directory. Business owners should be able to create, edit, and delete their own listings, including name, description, category, address, and coordinates. Users should be able to browse listings by location and category and submit or update one rating and review per business. Choose a suitable persistence layer, define the models and indexes, and implement the routes with input validation, pagination, ownership checks, and consistent errors. Include account authentication, aggregate ratings, setup instructions, and tests for the main flows.

title: Build concurrent card-number allocation
prompt: In this Go service, I need an endpoint that generates and persists unique 16–19 digit card numbers for a supplied IIN/BIN prefix and requested length, including a valid check digit. Use a relational database for durable storage and a shared key-value store for allocation state and card-number reservations under the supplied BIN key. Multiple app instances must handle concurrent requests without allocating duplicates; use atomic reservations or distributed locking and a database uniqueness constraint. Keep memory usage bounded rather than precomputing every possible number, and target allocation latency below 500 milliseconds under normal load. Return an explicit exhaustion error when a prefix's number space is depleted. Include tests for concurrent allocation, length and prefix validation, uniqueness, and exhaustion.

title: Persist employee records
prompt: In this employee management API, I need to persist employee objects to an embedded relational database using an object-relational mapper. Add an employee model with an ID, name, and department, plus endpoints to create an employee and retrieve one by ID. Include database initialization, input validation, and a test showing that saved records remain available after reopening the database.

title: Implement income and expense tracking
prompt: In my self-hosted personal finance app, I need a working Go example of the income and expense tracking module. Implement persistent transaction CRUD using a relational database, with fields for income or expense, amount, category, date, and an optional note. Add server-rendered pages to list, create, edit, and delete transactions, supporting partial HTML responses so forms and the list can update without a full page reload. Validate inputs, store money without floating-point rounding errors, and keep each user's transactions private. Include schema setup, tests for CRUD and user isolation, and local run instructions.

title: Implement court booking persistence and data access
prompt: In this API backing an Android court-booking app, I need persistent relational storage with entities, DAOs, and a database initialization class. Model user: id, username, password, name, lastname, age (int), sex (int), sport, bio; reservation: id, date, time, username, court, sport, equipment_required (bool); court: id, name, sport, rating (float). Other fields are strings except IDs. Store passwords securely as hashes. Link reservations to valid users and courts. Implement user add/edit/remove, reservation creation/list/detail/modification/cancellation, court availability checks for a date and time slot, and court rating updates. Reject conflicting bookings, including during modification, atomically. Expose API endpoints using the DAOs and add tests for persistence, relationships, booking conflicts, and cancellations.

title: Build a user account and ticket-hold API
prompt: In this Python FastAPI app, I need regular users to sign up, sign in, hold available tickets, and delete their accounts. Persist users, tickets, and holds in a document-oriented database. Store passwords securely and require authentication to create or release holds and delete an account. Prevent two users from holding the same ticket, let users view their own holds, and release their holds when they delete their account. Add tests for authentication, conflicting holds, ownership checks, and account deletion, plus local setup instructions using environment-based database configuration.

title: Document a Python database driver decision
prompt: In this Python API, I need Markdown Architectural Decision Records to choose a driver for a relational database. Inspect the starter and compare an asynchronous connection-pool adapter, a native asynchronous driver, a driver supporting both synchronous and asynchronous use, and any relevant alternatives. Cover API compatibility, pooling, transactions, performance, maintenance, and migration costs. Add the ADRs under docs/adr with context, alternatives, a recommended decision, and consequences. Clearly label assumptions and avoid unsupported performance claims.

title: Set up isolated local databases for commerce services
prompt: In this e-commerce backend, I'm at the database-creation step and want a lightweight embedded relational database for simplicity. Set up local databases for the product and order services, with each service owning its own database file and schema rather than sharing tables. Add repeatable schema initialization, minimal sample data, configurable file locations, and tests confirming persistence across restarts and isolation between services. Briefly document why this setup is suitable for local microservice development and its limitations for production. Keep the work limited to database setup; don't implement APIs, authentication, frontend pages, or deployment.

title: Add a product creation page with database persistence
prompt: In this Django app, I need a view page for adding a Product with Name, Text, and Image fields to a relational database. Please implement the model, form, view, route, and template using idiomatic practices and efficient database writes. Validate required fields and image uploads, store the image file with a reference on the product record, protect form submissions, display validation errors, and redirect after a successful save. Include tests for successful creation and invalid submissions.

title: Build a scalable pharmacy jobs backend
prompt: In this pharmacy jobs app, I've finished part of the frontend and need a backend. My proposed schema nests jobs and signup information under each user, then duplicates all jobs, pharmacists, and pharmacy technicians/assistants into large aggregate maps. Please improve this design for long-term use and implement persistent user profiles and jobs with clear ownership and consistent naming. Support pharmacist, technician, and assistant roles, profile updates, job creation and updates, and paginated job listings filtered by owner or role. Avoid unbounded aggregate records and unnecessary duplication. Add validation, tests, and a short explanation of the schema, indexes, and migration approach from my proposed structure.

title: Build a newsletter signup API
prompt: In this Express TypeScript API, I need a newsletter signup endpoint that accepts a required email address and an optional name. Persist subscriptions in a document database and return a JSON success flag after saving. Validate the email, reject invalid input with a clear error response, and handle repeat signups without creating duplicate subscriptions. Add tests for successful signup, missing or invalid email, optional name, and duplicate signup.

title: Build a recurring sports news collector
prompt: In this Python project, I need a program that collects the latest 10 sports news articles from a configurable news website and stores them in a persistent key-value database. Ask me for a positive polling interval n in hours, collect immediately, then repeat every n hours. Fetch each article page and store its headline, full news text, URL, publication date, and photo and video links when available. Do not save duplicate articles across polling cycles or program restarts. Handle failed requests without stopping future polls. Include configuration instructions and explain the setup and execution steps in order.

title: Build a scheduled sports-news importer
prompt: In this Python starter, I need a sports-news importer that accepts a news website URL and a positive polling interval n in hours from the user. Fetch the latest 10 sports articles immediately, then repeat every n hours. Visit each article page and store its URL, title, publication date, full news text, and photo and video links in a persistent document database. Prevent duplicate articles across polls and restarts using a stable article identifier or canonical URL. Handle network failures and missing fields without stopping future polls. Include tests for extraction and deduplication, and explain setup and execution steps in order.

title: Build a scheduled sports news collector
prompt: In this Python service, I need a collector that fetches the latest 10 articles from a configurable sports news website on startup and every 3 hours. Follow each article link and store its headline, full text, news URL, publication date, and photo URLs in a document database. Prevent duplicate articles across runs and restarts using a stable article identifier or canonical URL, with database-enforced uniqueness. Handle failed requests and malformed pages without stopping the entire collection. Add tests and explain the setup and execution steps in order.

title: Import multiple CSV files into a database
prompt: In this Python starter project, I need a command-line script that imports several .csv files into a relational database. Include an example using a fake directory such as /path/to/csv_files, discover all CSV files there, and load each into a table named after the file, using the header row as column names. Read database connection settings from environment variables, document how to run it, and report imported row counts and failures. Use a transaction per file so a failed import does not leave partial data.

title: Map product entities to document storage
prompt: In this product catalog API, I'm at the persistence-mapping step. I initially planned to map products to a table with a relational ORM, but the intended database stores documents. Please implement an appropriate document-based persistence layer in the existing starter. Model products with an ID, name, description, price, and availability, and provide repository methods to create, read, update, and delete them. Choose suitable tooling, configure the connection through environment variables, and explain how the mapping differs from a relational table mapping. Add tests for serialization, validation, and persistence behavior. Search, caching, monitoring, and deployment are later steps and out of scope.

title: Implement product catalog CRUD endpoints
prompt: In this product catalog API, I’m at the product-management CRUD step. Implement endpoints to create, list, retrieve, update, and delete products persisted in a document database. Each product should have an ID, name, description, price, and availability. Choose suitable persistence tooling and keep database access separate from request handlers. Validate required fields and nonnegative prices, return appropriate HTTP statuses for invalid input and missing products, and add tests covering successful CRUD operations and error cases. Document the database configuration and example API requests.

title: Build a game-history-driven tic-tac-toe bot
prompt: In this Next.js app, I want a website where I can play tic-tac-toe against a bot that learns from saved games. Choose and integrate persistent database storage rather than separate JSON files. Save each completed game's positions, moves, player marks, and outcome. On the bot's turn, query past games for that exact board position and choose the legal move with the most recorded wins for the bot's mark; if there is no winning history, choose a random legal move. Add a playable board, reject illegal moves, detect wins and draws, and provide tests for persistence and move selection. Keep the design simple enough for a first public project.

title: Design a searchable text-document catalog
prompt: In this FastAPI app, I want to organize decades of scattered text files in a relational database for a web interface. Please design and implement a suitable schema and API for importing, sorting, searching, filtering, and tagging documents. Support notes, designs, language-model prompts, image-generation prompts, wildcard lists whose entries can be randomly selected, and model reference pages containing descriptions, source links, and example prompts. Preserve original file paths and text, allow documents to have multiple categories and tags, and avoid silently duplicating files on reimport. Include schema setup, tests, and a short explanation of the modeling choices, search strategy, and considerations for large collections.

title: Build a local data-collection system simulator
prompt: I want to prototype a PC data-collection system entirely on my own machine before designing production deployment. In this starter app, build a mock ingestion API, a local relational database, a localhost webpage for querying and downloading collected records, and a local client simulator that generates sample machine data and posts it to the API. Let me configure the simulated client count, posting rate, and payload size to mimic thousands of PCs without needing those machines. Persist records, validate incoming data, and show request failures and basic throughput so I can explore overload behavior. Include setup instructions and a repeatable end-to-end test; no external services should be required.

title: Build a private document portal
prompt: In this Python web app, I need each user to register, log in, and upload and view their own documents. Use a database to persist accounts and document metadata, and store uploaded files durably. Add pages for login, upload, and a personal document list with links to view or download files. Require authentication and enforce ownership on every document request so users cannot access another user's files by guessing URLs. Include tests for login, uploads, and cross-user access denial.

title: Build a client-facing database API
prompt: I need other computers running Python clients to access a shared relational database through this Python service rather than connecting directly to the database. Design and implement a small server/client architecture: add authenticated API endpoints to create, list, and retrieve records, plus a Python client example that calls them over the network. Keep database credentials on the server, load connection settings from environment variables, use parameterized queries and managed connections, and document local setup, network access, and secure deployment. Include tests for successful requests, invalid input, and unauthorized access.

title: Build a POS app with persistent sales and inventory
prompt: In this POS web app, I need sales and stock management backed by a document database. Build a responsive interface for desktops and tablets with daily sales totals, category breakdowns, trend charts, and CSV/PDF report downloads. Support inventory search, filtering, sorting, item CRUD, low-stock thresholds and alerts, supplier refill orders, and a history of all stock movements. Recording a sale must update inventory consistently; expose REST endpoints for stock updates and optional supplier integrations. Add secure username/email-and-password login, sessions, and role-based permissions for managers, cashiers, and stock personnel. Keep UI, business logic, and persistence separate. Include unit and integration tests for reporting, inventory consistency, and permissions, plus API documentation, installation instructions, and a short user guide.

title: Build a live multiplayer fantasy draft
prompt: In this Express app, I want a live fantasy draft for current NBA players that multiple users can join from different devices. Build the frontend in three separate HTML, JavaScript, and CSS files, with multiple screens and a clean, modern dark theme. Let users create or join a draft, see available players and picks, and take turns drafting. Keep draft state synchronized across clients, prevent duplicate picks, and restore the draft after a refresh. I don't want to host the data myself, so use externally managed persistence with server-side credentials. Get current player data from an external API or scraping, and show clear loading and failure states. Document the required configuration and setup.

title: Build a purchase-wishlist PWA with analytics-ready storage
prompt: In this app, I want users to sign in with a mock/test login and submit descriptions of items they want to purchase. Start with a short PRD and implementation plan, then build a working PWA with an installable manifest, a submission form, and a page to view each user's requests. Choose a suitable persistence approach and separate users, purchase requests, item categories, and coarse geographic regions so backend analytics can identify regional demand trends. Validate submissions, keep users' requests isolated, and add a backend summary of request counts by category and region with tests. Avoid collecting precise location data.

title: Build a purchase-intent app with analytics-ready storage
prompt: In this starter app, I want a progressive web app where users can submit descriptions of items they intend to purchase; mock login is fine for now. Expand the idea into a short product requirements document and implementation plan, then build the core submission and history flows. Choose a persistence approach and separate users, purchase requests, item attributes, and coarse geographic data so backend analytics can aggregate demand by item category and region without parsing free text. Include validation, user-scoped access, sample data, and tests for persistence and geographic aggregation. Document your data-model decisions and provide an installable app shell with a useful offline fallback.

title: Persist port-scan progress and resume after crashes
prompt: In this Python port-checking app, I process a large ordered list of IP addresses, but results currently stay in memory and are exported to a spreadsheet only when I manually stop the run. Replace that workflow with database-backed persistence so each completed check is saved while the scan runs. Store the address, port, result, and position in the input list. On restart with the same list and port, resume after the last durably saved position without repeating completed checks. Keep the result and progress checkpoint consistent if the process crashes, and add tests for interrupted runs and resuming. Keep setup simple for someone learning Python and databases.

title: Build a school library manager with local persistence
prompt: In this Next.js starter, I want a desktop-ready high school library and archive manager used only by the school director. Choose suitable tools for an embedded local relational database, state management, and data fetching, and implement a well-structured app. Include first-launch account registration, a welcome page, login, and a statistics dashboard. Add book and student CRUD, student import from spreadsheet files, loan creation/deletion with open and completed views and statuses, and archive-record CRUD in a simple table. Every operational record must belong to a selectable school year; support adding and deleting years with safeguards against accidental data loss. Persist data across restarts and isolate views and statistics by year. Document the architecture, file layout, data-fetching flow, setup, and a path to packaging as a desktop app.

title: Build a school-year-aware library management app
prompt: In this Next.js starter, I want to build a desktop-ready high-school library and archive app used only by the school director, with a local relational database. Implement first-run account registration, welcome and login pages, and authenticated access. Let me create, select, and delete school years; all records and statistics must be scoped to the selected year. Add book and student CRUD, student import from spreadsheet files, loan creation/deletion with open and completed views and return status, and archive-record CRUD. Include dashboard summaries and a detailed statistics page. Design a SQL schema with keys, constraints, and safe year-deletion behavior. Organize the UI, data-access layer, and API fetching cleanly, with validation, transactions, loading/error states, and tests for year isolation and loan updates. Document setup and recommendations for local desktop packaging.

title: Build a city-based supplies management app
prompt: In this web app, I need a professional supplies dashboard with login and registration forms requiring username, password, and city. A master admin must approve registrations before accounts become active and manage cities through working add/edit/delete modals. Use a relational database with separate user, tool, and item tables for each city; automatically create, update, or remove the associated tables when cities change. Restrict users to their selected city's data. Let users add items with quantity fields for the current year, three preceding years, and next year, deriving labels dynamically. Predict next year's supply quantity from historical inputs using a documented method, and show a graph. Provide complete runnable code, setup instructions, secure password storage, a polished responsive UI, asynchronous form submissions, and searchable city dropdowns.

title: Build a database-backed Express API
prompt: In this TypeScript Express API starter, I need a server that connects to an existing relational database. Add environment-based connection settings and a reusable connection pool, then implement CRUD endpoints for a simple items table with id, name, and created_at fields. Include a schema setup script, input validation, parameterized queries, and safe error responses. Add a health endpoint that checks database connectivity and document how to configure and run the server locally.

title: Benchmark CSV files against database storage
prompt: In this HTTP server, I need to choose the faster way to serve prepared CSV content: returning a text file directly or fetching the identical CSV text from a local embedded relational database. Implement both paths and a reproducible benchmark using several payload sizes and concurrency levels. Keep response bytes and headers equivalent, separate setup costs from request timing, and test cold and warm reads. Report latency, throughput, and a recommendation based on the measurements rather than assumptions.

title: Build a minimal task management API
prompt: In this task-management app, I need a minimal, fully working REST API backed by a relational database. Add registration and login, and ensure users can only access their own tasks and categories. Tasks need a title, description, completed flag, creation date, and due date. Support creating, editing, deleting, and completing tasks, creating categories and assigning tasks to them, filtering by category and completion status, and sorting by creation or due date. Use Django with persistent data models. Keep the file structure small, avoid overengineering and unit tests, and include all essential code, dependency declarations, database setup, and run instructions. Use current compatible dependencies and comment anything a junior developer would find unclear.

title: Build a host-side meeting recorder with persistent history
prompt: In this Python meeting-recorder website, I want two tabs: Record and Past Meetings. Use only Python and HTML. Record audio on the machine running Python, not through browser capture. Let me start and stop recording and select microphone, desktop audio, or both (default); clearly report unavailable audio sources. Let me enter or edit a title before or after recording. While recording, let me save notes with elapsed timestamps, mark important moments, and add custom named segments to the recording timeline. Persist meeting metadata, notes, and segments in a local database file, with audio files stored on disk. In Past Meetings, show each recording's title, date, start and end clock times, playable/downloadable audio, timestamped notes, and segments. Keep saved meetings available after restarting the app.

title: Generate a modular motorcycle-shop bookkeeping system
prompt: In this Python bookkeeping project for a motorcycle maintenance company, I need a script that generates working modules: revenue_tracking.py for service income and parts/accessory sales; expense_management.py for vehicle maintenance, fuel, wages, benefits, rent, utilities, equipment and insurance; inventory_management.py for stock, usage and reorder levels; accounts_payable_receivable.py for supplier bills, customer invoices and payments; financial_reporting.py for profit/loss, balance sheets and cash flow; tax_compliance.py for taxable income and deductible expenses; and asset_management.py for assets, depreciation and financing. Generate main.py to integrate them. Use persistent database records, exact monetary arithmetic and validated transactions. Include tests and runnable sample workflows; reports must reconcile with recorded activity. Keep generated code modular and safe to regenerate.

title: Add user persistence and JWT synchronization
prompt: In this TypeScript API, I want to add a users table in a relational database and expose the current user through GraphQL. Implement the flow from a verified JWT to a persisted user: validate the token, use its subject as the unique external identity, and create or update the user from trusted profile claims on authenticated requests. Add a schema migration, a persistence layer, authentication middleware, and a current-user query. Reject invalid tokens, avoid duplicate users on concurrent requests, and keep internal user IDs stable. Include tests and a short explanation of the implementation steps and required configuration. Choose suitable tools that fit the starter.

title: Build a referentially complete SQL dump reducer
prompt: In this Python project, I need a script that reads a large relational database dump named example.sql from the current folder and writes reduced.sql. Aim to retain around 2% of the rows while preserving every table and its schema, including empty tables. Follow foreign-key references recursively so every retained row has all required referenced rows; referential integrity takes priority over the target percentage. Preserve Spanish characters and produce a valid, importable SQL dump. Handle large input without loading the entire dump into memory, document supported SQL syntax and usage, and add tests for chained and cyclic references, empty tables, and accented text.

title: Integrate a managed data service without replacing the backend
prompt: In this Express TypeScript REST API, I want to evaluate a managed database and authentication service without replacing the backend's business logic. Build a small authenticated records example with a configurable persistence adapter for a relational database. Keep validation and writes behind the API, verify externally issued access tokens, and restrict records to their owner. Include migrations, environment configuration, and tests for unauthorized access. Document how a separate TypeScript frontend can sign in and call the API, when direct database access is safe, and which responsibilities remain in the backend. Do not require live credentials to run tests.

title: Migrate issue-tracker persistence
prompt: In this Next.js issue-tracking app, I need to migrate the existing backend data integration to a document database. Review the database configuration, API routes, session middleware, and auth, workspace, member, project, and task features file by file, then update the affected code. Preserve existing UI behavior, authentication flows, workspace access controls, and relationships between records. Replace old data-access calls, document the required environment variables, and provide a migration script for existing records with stable IDs. Add tests for core CRUD operations and workspace isolation, and summarize the changed files.

title: Migrate project data to a document database
prompt: In this Next.js issue-tracking app, I want to replace the existing backend data service with a document database. The app has auth, members, projects, tasks, and workspaces features, database configuration, session middleware, and API routes. Inspect the starter and migrate the available persistence code while preserving feature behavior and workspace access controls. Update configuration, environment examples, and relevant setup scripts; remove obsolete backend dependencies. Show the updated folder structure and document the migration steps so I can apply changes file by file, including any data conversion needed.

title: Implement email and password authentication
prompt: In this Go HTTP service, I need email/password signup and login backed by an external identity provider, plus a browser frontend with signup and login forms. Implement backend endpoints that call the provider, validate input, and return safe authentication errors. Establish a secure session after successful authentication, add logout and a protected endpoint for the current user, and connect the frontend to these routes. Keep provider credentials in environment variables and never expose them to the browser. Include setup instructions and tests for successful authentication, invalid credentials, and unauthenticated access.

title: Build authentication and user profile panels
prompt: In this Django web app, I need registration, login, and logout, plus a protected account panel where users can view and edit their own profile and change their password. Add a public user directory with clickable profile pages showing only public profile fields, never credentials or private account details. Include a public comments section that anyone, including visitors, can post to. Validate form inputs, use secure password handling and CSRF protection, and ensure users cannot edit another user's account. Add tests covering authentication, account permissions, public profiles, and comments.

title: Build user accounts, profiles, and public comments
prompt: In this Django web app, I need registration, login, and logout backed by a relational database. Build HTML, CSS, and JavaScript pages with a private account panel where signed-in users can view and edit their own profile and change their password. Add a public user directory with clickable profile pages showing only public profile fields, plus a public comments section where any registered user can post after signing in. Enforce ownership checks, validate inputs, protect form submissions, and never expose passwords or private account details. Include tests for authentication, profile permissions, password changes, and comment posting.

title: Build authentication and user profile pages
prompt: In this Django web app, I need registration, login, logout, and authorization using a relational database and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript pages. Add a protected user panel where I can view and edit my own information and change my password after verifying my current password. Add a public user directory with clickable profiles showing only public information, plus a public comments section where any logged-in user can post. Validate inputs, protect form submissions, keep passwords securely hashed, and prevent users from editing another user's account. Include tests for access controls and the main account flows.

title: Build a secure authenticated todo app
prompt: In this Python starter project, I want to learn web development by building a todo app with authentication. Help me implement registration, login, logout, and creating, editing, completing, and deleting todos. Each user must only access their own todos. Use good practices for password storage, session security, input validation, and configuration. Add tests for authentication and access control, and explain the implementation step by step so I can learn as we build.

title: Build an authenticated todo app
prompt: In this Next.js starter, I want to build a todo app and understand how it works. Add registration, login, and logout with securely hashed passwords and persistent sessions. Let each signed-in user create, list, edit, complete, and delete only their own todos, enforcing ownership on the server. Persist users and todos in a relational database with a typed data-access layer and migrations. Include tests for authentication and user isolation, plus clear setup instructions and a walkthrough of the implementation.

title: Build simple sign-up and login forms
prompt: In this frontend app, I want simple, reusable sign-up and login components with clean, responsive styling using CSS utility classes. Keep the examples beginner-friendly: include labeled fields, password inputs, submit buttons, and a way to switch between the two forms. Add basic validation and show how submission handlers can connect to an authentication API without pretending a user has actually authenticated.

title: Build a secure login page
prompt: In this Django app, I need a login page backed by a relational database. Store only securely hashed passwords and verify them safely during login. Prevent SQL injection with parameterized queries, protect login submissions against CSRF, and rate-limit failed attempts by account and IP address. On successful login, establish a secure session and redirect to a protected page; include logout. Keep failure messages generic to avoid revealing whether an account exists. Add tests for valid and invalid credentials, injection attempts, missing CSRF tokens, and rate-limit enforcement.

title: Implement cookie-based JWT authentication
prompt: In this FastAPI service, I need JWT authentication for a separate browser frontend. Implement registration, login, logout, and a protected endpoint that returns the current user. Store passwords as secure hashes and send the JWT in an HttpOnly cookie rather than exposing it to frontend JavaScript. Configure cookie security, expiration, credentialed cross-origin requests, and CSRF protection for state-changing requests. Use environment-based secrets and allowed origins. Add tests for successful login, invalid credentials, expired tokens, logout, and unauthenticated access, plus a short example of browser requests that include cookies.

title: Build an authenticated channel gateway
prompt: In this gateway API, I need to accept requests from multiple channels and forward them to an upstream application's API. Authenticate each channel using a username and password, without tokens, and store passwords securely. Let me configure a separate requests-per-second limit for each channel and reject excess traffic with a clear rate-limit response. Add service-specific validation and a transformation layer that maps each valid request into the body expected by the upstream API. Keep channel limits, service rules, mappings, and upstream connection settings configurable. Handle authentication failures, invalid input, and upstream errors consistently, and add tests covering these behaviors.

title: Secure a dynamically configured microservice gateway
prompt: In this Express gateway, I want to secure access to three backend microservices for a browser frontend using OAuth2 and an external identity provider. Implement access-token validation using configurable issuer and audience settings and the provider's published signing keys. Keep routing dynamic: resolve backend destinations through a service registry and allow route configuration to reload without restarting. Reject missing, expired, or invalid tokens before forwarding requests, and preserve the authorization header for backend validation. Include tests, example configuration without secrets, and setup instructions explaining the frontend's authorization-code flow with PKCE and how backends should remain protected against direct access.

title: Plan and build ecommerce authentication
prompt: In this ecommerce app, I need a coherent 1-a/1-b implementation plan and a working authentication foundation. Use an n-tier design, a relational database, and documented, testable APIs. Build login/register screens, email activation, and many-to-many user/admin roles; only activated users may buy, and only admins may add products. Lock accounts after two failed logins and log failures in the database. Add a top-of-page Turkish/English toggle with localized validation. Plan carts, stock counts and atomic purchase decrements, order history, shipping with fake addresses, and emailed receipts. Ask for explicit consent before saving payment details; support multiple saved cards per user using provider tokens, never raw card data. Implement the auth flow first, with migrations and tests for activation, lockout, and role enforcement; keep email delivery configurable.

title: Add authentication, role checks, and request logging
prompt: In this ecommerce API, I want to turn my schema.sql design for users, products, cart_items, and orders into working routes backed by an embedded relational database. Users have usernames, passwords, email, names, and an is_admin flag; carts and orders reference users. Add registration, login, logout, and secure password hashing. Protect cart and order routes so users can access only their own records, and restrict product changes and order administration to admins. Public registration must not grant admin rights. Add request/response logging with method, path, status, and duration, without exposing passwords or authentication credentials. Include setup instructions and tests for unauthenticated access, ownership checks, and admin permissions.

title: Implement registration, login, and logout
prompt: In this web app with a Node.js backend and a document database, I need registration, login, and logout implemented in the existing Express API. Users must be able to log in with either email or username. Store email, a securely hashed password, username, avatar image reference, first name, last name, phone number, IP address history, wallet name, wallet ID, tasks completed, and join date. Validate registration data and enforce unique emails and usernames. Set join date and initial task count on the server, and record IP addresses from requests rather than user input. Add secure session handling, a current-user endpoint, and logout that invalidates the session. Never return password hashes. title: Implement user registration, login, and logout

prompt: In this Express app, I need a minimal webpage analytics system with a browser JavaScript tracker and a server endpoint that appends events to a .log file. Track visitor IP, referrer, page URL/title, browser/platform, available device details and screen resolution, language/timezone, clicks, scroll depth, and time on page. Support optional country/city/region lookup without requiring it to run. Only collect demographics when visitors explicitly provide them; don't infer age, gender, or interests. Include consent gating, input validation, safe concurrent log writes, and a demo page. Keep it lightweight and file-backed, with no database.

title: Build booking checkout with payment capture on approval
prompt: In this booking app, I need a checkout page where users select booking dates and enter payment details through a payment provider’s secure form. Submitting should create a pending booking and authorize payment without capturing it. Add an admin-only flow to confirm a booking and capture the authorized amount, or reject it and cancel the authorization. Handle expired authorizations and payment failures without marking bookings confirmed. Persist booking and payment status, verify provider callbacks, and prevent duplicate captures from repeated approvals or callbacks. Keep credentials server-side and never store raw card details.

title: Build booking payments with admin-approved capture
prompt: In this TypeScript Express service, I need a GraphQL API for booking requests with payments held pending until an admin confirms the booking. Implement a payment-provider integration that authorizes funds when a user requests a booking and captures them only after admin approval. Persist bookings and payment states in a relational database, restrict approval to admins, and release authorizations for rejected or canceled bookings. Handle expired authorizations, payment failures, duplicate approval requests, and verified provider callbacks without double charging. Use current stable tooling compatible with the starter, add tests, and document setup and the booking-to-payment flow. Keep payment credentials in environment variables and never store raw card details.

title: Build an ecommerce storefront with checkout
prompt: In this Next.js ecommerce app, I need a storefront that shows catalog items with prices and product details, plus user registration, sign-in, a shopping cart, checkout, payments, and order history. Persist users, products, carts, and orders. Integrate a payment provider in test mode, keep credentials server-side, calculate totals from stored prices, and only mark orders paid after verified payment confirmation. Handle declined payments and duplicate confirmations without creating duplicate orders. Include a seeded catalog, setup instructions, and tests for the main purchase flow.

title: Integrate installment payment checkout
prompt: In this Django storefront, I need to integrate an external installment payment provider. Keep the checkout controller, browser JavaScript file, and HTML template separate. Create checkout sessions server-side, launch the provider's checkout from the page, and show success, cancellation, and error states. Load credentials from environment variables and keep secrets out of browser code. Verify payment notifications before updating order status, handle duplicate notifications safely, and document the provider configuration needed.

title: Embed a web payment checkout
prompt: In my Flutter web app, I need to embed a payment provider's checkout script. Build a small TypeScript browser bridge that I can call through JavaScript interop. Load the provider's script only once, open checkout with the payment amount, currency, and order reference, and report success, cancellation, or errors back to the app. Keep provider configuration external, never expose server-side secrets, and include a minimal browser example and Flutter integration instructions.

title: Build checkout with reusable payment methods
prompt: In this checkout app, I want customers to pay within our own checkout flow instead of being redirected to a payment provider's premade page. Add a payment-provider integration that lets customers optionally save a payment method for future purchases and lets returning customers pay with a saved method. Use secure provider-managed collection so raw card details never reach our server; store only provider references and safe display details. Require explicit consent to save a method, restrict saved methods to their owner, and handle failed payments and any required customer verification. Include test-mode setup instructions and tests for these flows.

title: Build an image storefront with $1 purchases
prompt: In this Next.js app, I want a simple website titled "Attractive women over 60" where I can upload images for sale and visitors can buy each image for $1 USD. Add an owner-only upload page, a public gallery with previews, and checkout through a payment provider. Store image listings and purchase records, and let buyers download the original image only after payment is confirmed. Include a test checkout flow and setup instructions for the required credentials.

title: Build a shop bot with payments
prompt: In this Python app, I want a shop bot for a messaging platform. Load products from goods.txt, supporting either one line per product or a configurable number of lines per product, and document the file format. Show product images and inline buttons for browsing and buying. I'll supply the bot token and payment-provider token through environment variables. Implement webhook handling, invoice creation, checkout validation, and successful-payment confirmation. Only deliver purchased goods after confirmed payment, and handle duplicate payment notifications without delivering twice.

title: Implement verified miniapp credit purchases
prompt: In my Python FastAPI app, I need purchases using a messaging platform's virtual credits from a JavaScript miniapp. I already use WebSockets for full-duplex updates. Implement the backend payment flow and explain the architecture: create an invoice for an authenticated user and item, bind its payload to their UUIDs and a server-side order, and use the platform's bot API credentials and user ID to validate payment notifications. Never trust a client-reported success or exposed bot credentials. Check payer, amount, currency, and order; reject mismatches and fulfill each paid order exactly once despite duplicate callbacks or retries. Persist orders and transaction IDs, notify the user over WebSockets, and provide tests plus configuration instructions for the external payment integration.

title: Send payment lifecycle emails and expose booking references
prompt: In this TypeScript API, I need to email customers when a payment intent is created, when the payment is captured, and when it is refunded. Add a payment-provider webhook endpoint that verifies signatures, handles retries without sending duplicate emails, and records payment status against the booking. Use an email delivery provider with credentials supplied through environment variables. After checkout, my success page also needs the booking reference: provide a secure lookup endpoint using the checkout identifier from the redirect, since webhooks cannot pass data directly to the page. Handle the redirect arriving before the webhook, and add tests for these flows.

title: Build a temporary email inbox API
prompt: In this TypeScript Express service, I need a temporary email API for domains we control. Let clients discover available domains and generate an address, then receive incoming mail through an SMTP listener, parse it, and persist it in a database. Add endpoints to list messages by the address's login and domain, retrieve a message by ID as JSON with sender, recipients, subject, date, body, and attachment metadata, download attachments, and retrieve the original raw message encoded as base64. Reject mail for unsupported domains and ensure message and attachment lookups belong to the requested inbox. Include configuration, setup instructions, and tests covering ingestion and retrieval.

title: Send email using INI configuration
prompt: In this Python starter project, I need a command-line script that sends an email using settings from config.ini. Read To, CC, Subject, and Body from the file, along with configurable mail-server connection and authentication settings. Support multiple recipients and include CC recipients in delivery as well as the message headers. Provide a sample configuration with placeholders, keep credentials out of source code, and report missing settings or delivery failures clearly without exposing secrets.

title: Build a three-page chat app
prompt: In this Django app, I want a simple chat application with three pages: sign-in, account creation, and the chat room. Use Django’s built-in authentication for registration, login, and logout, and style all three pages with CSS. Only signed-in users should access the chat room. Let users send messages and see messages from other users without manually refreshing, showing each sender and timestamp. Persist messages, validate form input, and add tests for authentication and chat access.

title: Implement reliable hospital transaction event delivery
prompt: In this hospital transaction API, I need to prototype reliable event delivery for our legacy Java 8 system. Bills, receipts, advances, refunds, lab reports, and goods receipts must remain available when the message broker is down. Persist each transaction and its complete event payload atomically in a relational database, then publish pending events from a background worker and mark them delivered only after acknowledgment. Add retries with backoff, safe recovery after restarts, and stable event IDs so consumers can deduplicate deliveries. Downstream products need near-real-time updates when the broker is healthy. Include tests showing that broker outages do not block transactions and that queued events are delivered after recovery.

title: Add a WebSocket endpoint for mobile audio and photos
prompt: In my Python FastAPI server, I need a WebSocket endpoint that my phone app can connect to for uploading captured audio and photos. Add a protocol for sending media metadata and binary chunks, distinguish audio from photos, and save completed uploads locally with unique filenames. Acknowledge successful uploads and return clear errors for invalid messages or oversized uploads. Handle disconnects without leaving incomplete files behind. Include tests and a short protocol guide with example client messages so I can implement the phone app connection.

title: Build a mobile push notification API
prompt: In this Python API, I need to send push notifications to mobile devices through a push notification provider. Build an endpoint that accepts device tokens, a notification title and body, and optional custom data. Validate requests, keep provider credentials in environment configuration, and return clear delivery results, including invalid tokens and provider failures. Add tests with mocked delivery calls and document how to configure and run the API.

title: Build real-time crypto news alerts
prompt: In this Python service, I want to monitor news and exchange announcements for a configurable crypto coin and receive timely notifications on my smartphone that can also appear on my paired smartwatch. Add adapters for external news and exchange feeds, using streaming where available and frequent polling otherwise. Match coin names and symbols, deduplicate stories across feeds, and send alerts through a configurable notification channel. Keep credentials in environment variables, handle rate limits and transient failures, and test matching, deduplication, and notification delivery with mocked sources.

title: Build a secure invite-based chat and file-sharing app
prompt: In this web app, I need an invite link that immediately connects a joining user to the inviter in a private chat. Build a responsive desktop/mobile UI with a sidebar listing joined users, invite-link controls, and real-time text, image, file, and structured-data sharing. Use TypeScript, WebSocket communication, and encrypted peer-to-peer file transfers via WebRTC. Optimize large-file transfers with chunking and backpressure, showing progress, speed, cancellation, and clear connection failures. Protect invite tokens and restrict chat and transfer access to participants; encrypt messages and files in transit. Add a demo mode using generated sample files to measure actual transfer speed between two sessions. Include a step-by-step deployment guide for a hosted development environment, documenting secure transport and connectivity requirements.

title: Build a synchronized two-player Tic-Tac-Toe game
prompt: In this web app, I want two players in different browsers to play Tic-Tac-Toe in real time. Build a grid-based UI with separate HTML, CSS, and client JavaScript files, backed by a Node.js server using WebSocket communication. Let players create or join a game, assign their marks, enforce turns and legal moves on the server, and synchronize the board, turn, win/loss/draw result, and restart state between both clients. Include a restart option, clear connection and error messages, and handling for disconnects so a player cannot keep making moves while their opponent is offline.

title: Build a real-time Tic-Tac-Toe app
prompt: In this TypeScript Express app, I need a browser-based Tic-Tac-Toe game with a polished, responsive interface. Add username/password registration and login with hashed passwords and signed authentication tokens. Store users, game records, and results in JSON files. Build a dashboard showing games played, won, and lost, plus a leaderboard ranked by wins. Let authenticated users enter a matchmaking queue and pair them with another waiting player. Use WebSockets for live gameplay across browsers, enforcing turns and legal moves on the server, detecting wins and draws, and updating both players immediately. Handle duplicate queue entries and disconnects gracefully, and persist completed results without counting them twice.

title: Build targeted social messaging and engagement tracking
prompt: In this Python FastAPI app, I need to integrate with a social platform API to find eligible recipients by keywords, hashtags, or location and send personalized direct messages from predefined templates. Add endpoints to manage templates, preview recipient matches and rendered messages, and launch messaging campaigns. Persist delivery status and replies, and report response rates and engagement metrics per campaign. Keep API credentials configurable, respect platform messaging permissions and rate limits, and prevent duplicate sends when requests are retried.

title: Build a live image display with an upload page
prompt: In this Python web app, I need two pages: a fullscreen display showing the current image and an upload page where I can replace it. When an upload succeeds, every open display page should update in real time without a manual refresh. Keep the image fitted to the screen without distortion. Validate uploads as images, show clear success or error feedback, and retain the latest image across server restarts. Choose an appropriate way to notify connected displays, and ensure newly opened or reconnected displays show the latest image.

title: Build a real-time chat app
prompt: In this chat app, I need a TypeScript backend and a browser UI for private messaging, group chats, and real-time notifications. Let users choose a display name, start a private conversation, create or join a group, and send messages that appear immediately for connected participants. Show unread-message notifications outside the active conversation, retain conversation history across reloads, and handle disconnects and reconnects without duplicating messages. Choose suitable communication and persistence tools, and include tests plus local setup instructions.

title: Build fluency-matched voice rooms
prompt: In this backend for a gamified Android English-learning app, I need users to choose their speaking-fluency level at login and meet learners at the same level in a shared map-like world. Implement APIs to save fluency, join a matching room, and track avatar positions, plus real-time presence and signaling for live peer-to-peer voice chat. Handle disconnects and prevent cross-level room joins. Favor free, self-hostable tools without requiring paid accounts. Include tests and documentation covering the Android client integration, local setup, and network requirements and limitations for voice calls.

title: Implement a booking waitlist API
prompt: In this Express API, I need an exported async addToWaitlist handler accepting userId, checkInDate, checkOutDate, and roomId. Read the existing booking models and routes before wiring it in. Validate required fields and date ranges, reject conflicting bookings or duplicate entries, and add users only when the requested room dates are fully booked. Persist the date range, roomId, userId, and priority in a document database. When a booking is canceled, notify eligible waitlisted users in priority order and offer the available slot. Return a success confirmation and handle validation and database failures clearly. Include comments explaining the availability and notification logic.

title: Build low-latency orderbook workers and an aggregator
prompt: In this Python market-data service, I need code for multiple worker servers and a main aggregation server. Each worker fetches orderbooks for 60 assigned coins from a configurable market-data API and forwards updates to the main server. I want to minimize the interval between consecutive fetches for each coin and deliver the latest prices quickly, while respecting per-IP rate limits and the provider's access rules. Implement configurable concurrency, rate-limit handling, retries, and a low-latency messaging transport. The main server should retain the newest orderbook per coin, reject stale or duplicate updates, and expose current snapshots. Include configuration for coin assignments and endpoints, worker reconnection and bounded buffering, tests with a fake upstream API, and instructions for running workers and the main server separately.

title: Enforce a global file-operation rate limit
prompt: In this TypeScript Express API, users can upload, view, and download files through an existing object-storage adapter. I need to cap these interactions at 400 per second total across all users, not per user. Implement shared rate coordination that remains correct across multiple API workers, queuing excess operations rather than dropping them. Preserve upload/view/download behavior, expose queued-operation status if requests cannot complete immediately, and add tests proving the combined limit holds under concurrent traffic. Choose appropriate coordination and background-job tools.

title: Schedule a daily midnight job
prompt: In this Go service, I need a scheduler that calls a function every day at 12:00 AM. Add a configurable timezone, defaulting to UTC, and wire it into the service lifecycle so scheduling starts with the service and stops cleanly on shutdown. Prevent overlapping runs if the function is still executing at the next scheduled time, and log failures without stopping future runs. Include tests for calculating the next midnight and for shutdown behavior, without making tests wait until midnight.

title: Implement queued per-client task processing
prompt: In this Python server, I need requests and responses processed through queues rather than returning task results immediately. Implement an API that accepts a client ID and task request, returns an acknowledgment with a job ID, and lets clients retrieve queued responses later. Maintain a separate worker thread for each active client and preserve that client's request order. Internal tasks may be synchronous functions or asynchronous coroutines; support both without blocking request handling. Include bounded queues, task failure reporting, idle worker cleanup, graceful shutdown, and tests covering client isolation and both task types. Briefly document the architecture and its limitations.

title: Add distributed task queue management
prompt: In this Python API service, I need a task queue management module that distributes background tasks across available worker servers with load balancing. Add endpoints to enqueue tasks and check their status, plus a worker entry point. Track worker availability and load so tasks go to healthy workers with spare capacity. Support bounded retries and recovery when a worker disconnects without silently losing tasks. Include tests for dispatch, load balancing, and worker failure, and document how to run the API with multiple workers locally.

title: Build a scheduled-job microservice
prompt: In this service, I want to build a scheduling microservice for my existing web app. Add administrative endpoints to add, stop, start, remove, and list scheduled jobs, plus list available job types. Jobs should accept cron-style schedules. Define interfaces for implementing job types and creating child jobs. Include an example job that finds accounts exceeding their limits and creates one child job per account to email its statement to the owner. Keep account lookup and email delivery behind replaceable interfaces. Persist schedules and job status across restarts, distinguish stopping future runs from cancelling active work, and test scheduling, lifecycle operations, and child-job creation.

title: Build a scheduled-job management service
prompt: I need a scheduled-job microservice for my existing app. Build admin endpoints to add, stop, start, remove, and list scheduled jobs, plus list available job types with a customizable flag and default cron expression. Define an extensible interface for registering job types and creating child jobs. Include a job that runs on an admin-specified cron schedule, finds accounts that exceeded their limits, and queues one child job per account to email its statement to the owner. Persist schedules and job state, validate cron input, and ensure stopped jobs do not run. Include tests and example requests showing the parent/child workflow.

title: Build safe scheduled plugin updates across CMS sites
prompt: In this Node.js backend, I need to manage plugin updates for multiple CMS websites hosted on subdomains of the same shared-hosting account. Build a configurable site registry and authenticated endpoints to inspect installed plugin versions and trigger updates across all sites. Also provide a cron-invokable command that checks versions and updates outdated plugins without requiring a persistent worker. Keep orchestration entirely in the backend, using each site's authenticated management interface and validating request nonces where required. Back up affected files and database state before updating; skip updates if backups fail, verify site health afterward, and support rollback. Prevent overlapping runs, isolate per-site failures, and record per-plugin results. Include tests with simulated site responses and setup instructions covering hosting permissions, credentials, and scheduling.

title: Build a monolithic image-processing API with background workers
prompt: In my worker CRM, users upload up to 500 history-sheet images at once. My pipeline removes backgrounds in Python, then runs four JavaScript processing stages that call an AI image-analysis API. Separate services and queues between stages have made it slow and fragile. I want a Go monolith with an upload API and a configurable pool of background workers that run the whole pipeline. Implement batch submission, job status and per-image results, bounded concurrency, retries, and persistent job state so restarts don't lose work. Integrate the Python background-removal step and existing JavaScript stages through clear adapters. Keep API requests responsive and failures isolated per image. Document the architecture, configuration, and how to deploy the API and workers together on one host.

title: Scaffold a self-hosted uptime management app
prompt: In this self-hosted uptime management app, Upfinity, I want a complete repository scaffold with a modern, polished web UI and public status pages. Organize it for configurable monitors, recurring uptime checks, incident history, custom domains for status pages, email and SMS alerts, and an API for managing monitors and retrieving status. All features should be available without paywalls. Provide a full project tree listing every individual file, including files inside nested folders, with no placeholders or omitted sections. Create the corresponding files with meaningful starter code and document how to run the app locally and self-host it, including configuration for alert delivery and custom domains.

title: Add cluster monitoring and availability checks
prompt: In this Go monitoring service, I want to monitor all containers in my clustered container deployment, which sits behind a reverse proxy. Add a dashboard showing per-container CPU, memory, and network usage, plus availability and response times for configurable web app URLs. Choose suitable monitoring components and include deployment configuration for collecting metrics from every cluster node, retaining history, and exposing the dashboard through the existing proxy. Keep monitoring credentials configurable, restrict dashboard access, and document setup, required permissions, and how to verify metrics collection and detect an unavailable app.

title: Add browser error monitoring to the payment form
prompt: In this server-rendered payment app, I need to load and initialize a browser error-monitoring SDK on the payment form. I tried adding a module import directly to the HTML template, but it does not work. Choose a suitable integration and wire it into the existing page so uncaught browser errors are reported to a configurable monitoring endpoint. Keep browser-only code out of server execution, document the configuration, and exclude payment details from error reports.

title: Build an internal service status dashboard
prompt: In this internal service status app, I want a dashboard that groups services by owner-selected category, with browser-side search and filtering by service status. Clicking a service should open a detail card showing its support chat channel, current alerts, recent incidents, and an action to create an incident. Build a self-service area in the same app where service owners can onboard services and edit their category, status, and support details. Persist service registrations, alerts, and incidents so the dashboard and owner views stay consistent. Include sample data and clear loading, empty, and error states.

title: Build an embeddable server monitoring dashboard
prompt: I need a monitoring panel that integrates into our existing Java-based admin dashboard, not a separately installed monitoring application. In this Next.js starter, build an embeddable panel showing server CPU usage, memory usage, active session count, a quick log scan, and recent exceptions. Choose suitable visualization tools and define a data adapter for metrics and logs from our Java server; include sample data so we can test without connecting it. For now, show attractive, non-interactive graphs that refresh periodically, with no configuration or drill-down controls. Structure the implementation so we can later add real-time updates, drill-downs, and cursor-based inspection of graph points. Document how to embed the panel and connect the server data.

title: Embed a server monitoring dashboard
prompt: In this Next.js app, I need an embeddable monitoring panel for our existing Java-based admin dashboard, not a separately installed monitoring application. Show server CPU and memory usage, active session count, a quick log summary, and recent exceptions. Integrate with a configurable metrics endpoint and include sample data for local development. Choose an existing visualization tool rather than building charts from scratch, with simple branding overrides. title: Embed server monitoring charts in the admin dashboard
prompt: In this app, I need an embeddable monitoring panel for our Java server's existing admin dashboard, not a separately installed dashboard. title: Embed server monitoring in the admin dashboard
prompt: In this Next.js app, I need an embeddable monitoring view for our existing Java-based admin dashboard, not a separately installed monitoring application. Show CPU usage, memory usage, active session count, a quick log scan, and recent exceptions. Choose an existing visualization tool rather than building chart rendering from scratch, with minimal integration work and branding overrides. The chosen approach must also support a later phase with live updates, drill-downs, and cursor-based inspection of graph values. title: Add containerized observability to the prediction API
prompt: In my FastAPI app, I serve a saved logistic regression model trained on a passenger survival dataset with about 83% accuracy. I want to add observability using only open-source components that can run in containers. Instrument prediction requests with structured logs, metrics, and distributed traces, including request latency, error counts, and model inference duration. Avoid logging passenger inputs. Add a local container setup with a dashboard and an example alert for elevated errors, plus instructions to generate test traffic and verify the telemetry. Keep the existing prediction endpoint working.

title: Add distributed API rate limiting
prompt: In this API service, I need rate limits to apply across all container replicas, not separately in each process. Implement a token-bucket limiter backed by a shared cache, with atomic updates so concurrent requests to different replicas cannot exceed the limit. Add a simple rate-limited endpoint, configurable bucket capacity and refill rate, and per-client limits. Return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header when exhausted. Include setup instructions for running two instances against the same cache and tests demonstrating that they share one limit. Explain how the limiter and shared cache work together.

title: Implement configurable distributed API rate limiting
prompt: In this TypeScript Express API, I need a working example of distributed rate limiting across multiple application replicas. Load per-endpoint token-bucket settings from a spreadsheet, with columns for HTTP method, path, capacity, and refill rate, and allow configuration reloads without restarting. Use a shared cache to coordinate consumption atomically so concurrent requests across replicas cannot exceed the configured limits. Return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header when a bucket is exhausted. Handle invalid configuration and cache timeouts explicitly, and include tests for endpoint-specific limits, refills, reloads, and concurrent consumption, plus setup instructions.

title: Add cache-backed API rate limiting
prompt: In this TypeScript Express API, I want a simple example of rate limiting backed by a running external key-value cache. Add an example endpoint and middleware that allows 10 requests per client IP per minute, returning HTTP 429 when the limit is exceeded. Use atomic counter updates and expiration so limits work across multiple API instances. Configure the cache connection through environment variables for host, port, and optional credentials. Include setup instructions, example configuration, and tests for allowed requests, rejected requests, and window expiration.

title: Add reusable API response caching middleware
prompt: In this TypeScript Express API, I want reusable middleware that caches responses from read endpoints backed by a document database so repeated requests avoid querying the database. Let me enable caching per route with a configurable TTL. Use a shared key-value cache, build keys from the request path and query parameters, and cache only successful responses. Ensure user-specific responses cannot leak between users and let requests proceed normally if the cache is unavailable. Apply it to an existing read endpoint, add tests for hits, misses, expiration, and cache failures, and document setup and usage.

title: Replace map-based caching with a shared cache
prompt: In this API, I currently cache data in in-memory maps. Replace that approach with a shared network-accessible key-value cache so multiple application instances can reuse cached data. Preserve the existing lookup behavior, add configurable entry expiration and connection settings, and fall back to loading the original data if the cache is unavailable. Keep cache access behind a small abstraction and add tests for cache hits, misses, expiration, and connection failures.

title: Cache AI responses before making upstream requests
prompt: In this TypeScript service, I need to cache AI API responses by user query. Before sending an upstream request, check the cache and return any unexpired matching response. On a miss, call the AI API and cache the successful result with a configurable expiration time. Include response-affecting options in the cache key so different requests do not share incorrect results. Do not cache failures, and keep API credentials out of cache keys and logs. Choose a suitable caching approach and add tests for hits, misses, expiration, and upstream errors.

title: Build a horizontally scalable word game backend
prompt: In this FastAPI web service, I need a WebSocket word game with one shared daily word randomly chosen from a word list and five guesses per user. Store active sessions in a shared cache and use distributed locks so concurrent requests across instances cannot consume guesses or finish a session twice. Generate a deterministic session UUID from the word, date, and user UUID. Persist only final win/loss results in a database. On a win, publish a points-claim message to a configurable message-broker topic using the session UUID as the idempotency key. Support reconnects without resetting guesses, and test concurrency, session identity, and duplicate win handling.

title: Add a cached session hook
prompt: In this TypeScript browser-extension app using manifest version 3, I already have an async getSession function that fetches the current authentication session from the server. Implement a useSession hook that synchronously returns the latest cached session and refreshes it only after a configurable interval. Share the cache across hook consumers and deduplicate concurrent requests. Also call getSession whenever the user closes or opens the modal, bypassing the refresh interval. Handle loading and failures, and clean up event listeners on unmount.
